literal: The princess's aunt Princess of Chenliu together wielded fans to encourage them, and with Hui again came to angry quarrel.
idiomatic: Her aunt Princess of Chenliu fanned the affair on, and Hui quarreled with the princess again.

literal: Hui pushed the princess from the bed and beat and trampled her hands and feet; the princess thus miscarried.
idiomatic: Hui threw her from the bed and trampled her; she miscarried.

literal: Hui, fearing punishment, fled.
idiomatic: Fearing punishment, Hui fled.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling summoned Prince of Qinghe Yi to decide the affair.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling summoned Prince Yi of Qinghe to judge.

literal: The two families' daughters were shaved and flogged at the palace assembly; the brothers were all punished with the whip.
idiomatic: The Zhang and Chen daughters were shaved and flogged at court; their brothers were whipped.

literal: They were banished to Dunhuang as soldiers.
idiomatic: They were sent to Dunhuang as soldiers.

literal: The princess died from her wounds; the empress dowager came in person to mourn and weep, and mourning was raised at the eastern hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
idiomatic: The princess died of her wounds; the empress dowager mourned at the eastern hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

literal: Burial was outside the western wall; the empress dowager escorted several li and returned only when grief was spent.
idiomatic: Buried outside the west wall; the empress dowager escorted her several li and returned in grief.

literal: Later Hui was seized at Wen in Henei, imprisoned in Si Province, and was to receive the death penalty.
idiomatic: Later Hui was taken at Wen in Henei, held in Si Province, and marked for death.

literal: An amnesty came and he was spared.
idiomatic: An amnesty spared him.

literal: Later his office and title were restored; he was moved to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Regular Attendant, and died—the house then declined.
idiomatic: Later rank was restored; he was General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Regular Attendant, then died—the house faded.

literal: Xiao Baoyin, styled Zhiliang, was the sixth son of Emperor Ming of Qi, younger brother of the mother of the deposed emperor Baojuan.
idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin, styled Zhiliang, was Qi Emperor Ming's sixth son, younger brother of deposed Emperor Baojuan's mother.

literal: In Qi he was enfeoffed Prince of Jian'an.
idiomatic: In Qi he was Prince of Jian'an.

literal: When Emperor He of Qi took the throne, he was changed to Prince of Poyang.
idiomatic: When Emperor He acceded he was made Prince of Poyang.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang took Jiankang, troops guarded him and were about to harm him.
idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Wu took Jiankang, guards were set to kill him.

literal: His household eunuch Yan Wenzhi with attendants Ma Gong and Huang Shen secretly plotted, broke through the wall by night, and brought Baoyin out.
idiomatic: Eunuch Yan Wenzhi with Ma Gong and Huang Shen broke through the wall at night and stole him out.

literal: They prepared a small boat on the riverbank; they stripped his formal dress and put on a black cloth jacket;
idiomatic: A small boat waited on the bank; they stripped his robes for a black cloth jacket;

literal: at the waist he tied more than a thousand cash and stole to the riverbank;
idiomatic: he tied a thousand-odd cash at his waist and stole to the shore;

literal: treading sandals he went on foot; his feet had no whole skin.
idiomatic: in sandals he walked until his feet had no whole skin.

literal: The guards pursued at dawn.
idiomatic: Guards pursued at dawn.

literal: Baoyin pretended to be a fisherman, drifting up and down the stream more than ten li; the pursuers did not suspect.
idiomatic: He played fisherman, drifting ten li; pursuers passed him by.

literal: When they dispersed, he then crossed to the west bank.
idiomatic: When they broke off he crossed to the west bank.

literal: He then entrusted his life to Hua Wenrong.
idiomatic: He then cast himself on Hua Wenrong.

literal: Wenrong with his followers Tianlong, Huilian, and three others abandoned their families, hid Baoyin in mountain ravines, hired donkeys to ride, lay by day and marched by night.
idiomatic: Wenrong with Tianlong, Huilian, and three others abandoned home, hid him in the hills, rode hired donkeys, and marched by night.

literal: In the second year of Jingming he reached the eastern-wall garrison of Shouyang.
idiomatic: Jingming year 2 he reached Shouyang's eastern garrison.

literal: Garrison chief Du Yuanlun examined him and knew he was truly a son of the Xiao house; he received him with ritual courtesy.
idiomatic: Garrison chief Du Yuanlun identified a true Xiao prince and received him with ceremony.

literal: He sent word in haste to Yang Province Inspector, Prince of Rencheng Cheng.
idiomatic: He reported at once to Yang Inspector Prince Cheng of Rencheng.

literal: Cheng came with carriage, horses, and guards to welcome him.
idiomatic: Cheng came with carriage, horses, and escort.

literal: He was then sixteen; on foot, haggard and worn, viewers thought him a kidnapped slave being sold.
idiomatic: Sixteen, on foot and haggard, onlookers took him for a sold captive.

literal: Cheng received him with guest rites.
idiomatic: Cheng treated him as a guest.

literal: He then asked for the hemp mourning of a murdered lord; Cheng sent men to explain the proper feeling and ritual, and in the rites for a murdered elder brother gave him the hemp of the next degree; Baoyin obeyed.
idiomatic: He asked for hemp mourning for a slain sovereign; Cheng explained ritual and gave him second-degree hemp for a slain elder brother; Baoyin obeyed.

literal: Cheng led the officials to offer condolence.
idiomatic: Cheng led officials to mourn.

literal: Baoyin's dwelling had ritual propriety; he did not drink wine or eat meat;
idiomatic: Baoyin lived with ritual; no wine or meat;

literal: he ceased laughter and spoke briefly, all one with the utmost of mourning.
idiomatic: he ceased laughter and spoke little, in utmost mourning.

literal: In Shouyang many of his old associates came; all received his comfort and condolence.
idiomatic: Many old associates in Shouyang came; he received them in mourning.

literal: Only he did not see the Xiahou clan, because they were of Liang.
idiomatic: He avoided the Xiahous, being Liang men.

literal: Another day he visited Cheng; Cheng deeply valued him.
idiomatic: Another day he called on Cheng, who prized him deeply.

literal: When he reached the capital, Emperor Xuanwu honored him heavily.
idiomatic: At the capital Xuanwu honored him greatly.

literal: He prostrated himself below the palace gate and begged troops for a southern campaign; though violent wind and heavy rain came, he never moved for a moment.
idiomatic: He knelt at the gate begging troops south; through storm he did not stir.

literal: That year Liang's Inspector of Jiangzhou Chen Bozhi with his chief clerk Chu Zhou and others returned from Shouyang to surrender and asked to lead an army for merit.
idiomatic: That year Liang's Jiang Inspector Chen Bozhi with Chu Zhou surrendered from Shouyang offering service.

literal: The emperor said that what Bozhi reported could not be lost in time.
idiomatic: The emperor said Bozhi's offer could not wait.

literal: Because Baoyin was earnest and sincere, he was made Commissioner with credentials, Area Commander, Inspector of Eastern Yang, General Who Pacifies the East, Duke of Danyang, Prince of Qi, with ten thousand troops assigned, ordered to hold the eastern wall and await the great stroke in autumn and winter.
idiomatic: For his earnestness he was Commissioner, eastern commander, Eastern Yang Inspector, General Who Pacifies the East, Duke of Danyang, Prince of Qi, with ten thousand men at the eastern wall till autumn's campaign.

literal: The night before he was to receive the appointment he wept in anguish.
idiomatic: The night before investiture he wept in anguish.

literal: At dawn the full ritual of investiture was prepared; carriage, horses, and objects were granted; the affair was rich and thick, yet still not equal to Liu Chang's exceptional favor.
idiomatic: At dawn full investiture came with rich gifts—yet still short of Liu Chang's favor.

literal: He was also allowed to recruit valiant men throughout the realm and got several thousand.
idiomatic: He was allowed to recruit braves and gathered thousands.

literal: Wenzhi and the other three were made generals of powerful crossbows; Wenrong and the other three were made generals of strong crossbows, all as army commanders.
idiomatic: Wenzhi's three became powerful-crossbow generals; Wenrong's three strong-crossbow generals—all army commanders.

literal: Though Baoyin was young and long a hostage, his will and nature were elegant and weighty.
idiomatic: Young and long exiled, his will was still elegant and grave.

literal: Past the mourning term he still abstained from wine and meat; his face was haggard, he ate vegetables and coarse cloth and never laughed.
idiomatic: Past mourning he still abstained; haggard, in vegetables and coarse cloth, he never laughed.

literal: When ordered to campaign south, the great and powerful relied on him in multitudes; his gate was like a market of guests.
idiomatic: Ordered south, the powerful crowded his gate like a market.

literal: Yet letters followed one another and Baoyin answered and replied without losing reason.
idiomatic: Letters piled up; he answered each without losing reason.

literal: In the first year of Zhengshi, Baoyin reached Ruyin; the eastern wall had fallen, so he stopped at Shouyang's Qixian Temple.
idiomatic: Zhengshi year 1 he reached Ruyin; the eastern wall had fallen, so he halted at Shouyang's Qixian Temple.

literal: He met Liang general Jiang Qingzhen invading within; Qingzhen besieged Shouyang.
idiomatic: Liang's Jiang Qingzhen invaded and besieged Shouyang.

literal: Baoyin led the crowd in fierce battle and routed him.
idiomatic: Baoyin fought hard and routed him.

literal: Baoyin's courage topped the armies; those who heard and saw were all stirred.
idiomatic: His courage topped the armies; all who saw were stirred.

literal: On return he was changed to Duke of Liang Commandery.
idiomatic: On return he was made Duke of Liang Commandery.

literal: When Prince of Zhongshan Ying campaigned south, Baoyin again memorialized asking to campaign.
idiomatic: When Prince Ying of Zhongshan marched south Baoyin again asked to go.

literal: With Ying he repeatedly defeated Liang armies and pressed the attack on Zhongli.
idiomatic: With Ying he repeatedly beat Liang and pressed Zhongli.

literal: The Huai overflowed; Baoyin and Ying withdrew in disorder; soldiers drowned and perished—four or five in ten.
idiomatic: The Huai flooded; Baoyin and Ying fled in disorder; four or five in ten drowned.

literal: The offices memorialized that he should receive the extreme penalty.
idiomatic: Offices asked the extreme penalty.

literal: An edict pardoned death; he was dismissed from office, stripped of title, and returned to his house.
idiomatic: An edict spared death, stripped office and rank, and sent him home.

literal: Soon he married the Princess of Nanyang.
idiomatic: Soon he married the Princess of Nanyang.

literal: The princess had wifely virtue; Baoyin fully observed harmonious rites; though fond of her, his respectful service did not slacken.
idiomatic: The princess was virtuous; he kept full harmony; fond yet never slack in respect.

literal: Whenever Baoyin entered the chamber the princess always stood to await him; they met like guests; unless the queen mother's illness was grave he never retired to rest.
idiomatic: When he entered she stood; they met as guests; unless the queen mother was gravely ill he never rested within.

literal: Baoyin's disposition was gentle and compliant; he placed himself within ritual, revered the princess, and inside and outside were sheltered in harmony.
idiomatic: Gentle and compliant, he kept ritual, revered her, and household and court were at peace.

literal: Prince of Qinghe Yi was kin and valued him.
idiomatic: Prince Yi of Qinghe was kin and prized him.

literal: In the fourth year of Yongping, Lu Chang took Liang's Zhushan garrison; Langye garrison chief Fu Wenji guarded it.
idiomatic: Yongping year 4 Lu Chang took Liang's Zhushan; Langye chief Fu Wenji held it.

literal: Liang's army attacked Wenji; Chang supervised the mass of armies to rescue him.
idiomatic: Liang attacked Wenji; Chang led the host to relieve him.

literal: An edict made Baoyin Commissioner with credentials and acting General Who Pacifies the South, a separate commander driving deep to the rescue, under Chang's command.
idiomatic: Baoyin was Commissioner and acting General Who Pacifies the South, a separate column under Chang.

literal: Receiving the edict, tears streamed; he choked for a long while.
idiomatic: Receiving the edict he wept and choked long.

literal: Later Chang's army was defeated; only Baoyin brought the whole army back intact.
idiomatic: Later Chang was beaten; only Baoyin brought the army back whole.

literal: At the beginning of Yanxi he was made Inspector of Ying, restored as Prince of Qi, and moved to Inspector of Ji.
idiomatic: Yanxi's start made him Ying Inspector, restored Prince of Qi, then Ji Inspector.

literal: When the Mahayana rebels rose, Baoyin sent troops to attack them and was repeatedly beaten by the rebels.
idiomatic: When Mahayana rebels rose he sent troops and was repeatedly beaten.

literal: When the capital army arrived, they were then destroyed.
idiomatic: When the capital army came they were destroyed.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling held court and he returned to the capital.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling held court; he returned to the capital.

literal: Liang general Kang Xuan at Fushan dammed the Huai to flood Yang and Xu.
idiomatic: Liang's Kang Xuan dammed the Huai at Fushan to flood Yang and Xu.

literal: Baoyin was made Commissioner with credentials, Area Commander of the Eastern Expedition, General Who Pacifies the East, to attack him, and again enfeoffed Duke of Liang Commandery.
idiomatic: Baoyin was eastern commander and General Who Pacifies the East against him, again Duke of Liang Commandery.

literal: At the beginning of Xiping, when Liang's dam was complete and the Huai was about to become a calamity for Yang and Xu, Baoyin cut a new channel above the dam and the water lessened somewhat.
idiomatic: Xiping's start: Liang's dam threatened Yang and Xu; Baoyin cut a channel above it and eased the flood.

literal: He then sent more than a thousand stalwarts by night across the Huai, burned their bamboo-and-wood camps, broke three fortresses, and fires burned for days without going out.
idiomatic: He sent a thousand men by night across the Huai, burned bamboo camps, broke three forts; fires burned for days.

literal: He also sent separate commanders to defeat Liang generals Yuan Mengsun and Zhang Sengfu north of the Huai.
idiomatic: Separate columns defeated Liang generals Yuan Mengsun and Zhang Sengfu north of the Huai.

literal: He then crossed south of the Huai and burned eleven camps of Liang's Inspector of Xuzhou Zhang Baozi and others.
idiomatic: He crossed south and burned eleven camps of Liang's Xu Inspector Zhang Baozi and others.

literal: On return to the capital he was made Director of the Palace Department.
idiomatic: Back at court he was Director of the Palace Department.

literal: While Baoyin was at the Huai dam, Emperor Wu of Liang sent a letter lodged to entice him.
idiomatic: At the Huai dam Liang's Emperor Wu sent a letter to entice him.

literal: Baoyin memorialized forwarding the letter and stated his bitter, poisonous intent.
idiomatic: Baoyin forwarded the letter and declared his bitter resolve.

literal: His will was set on wiping away shame; he repeatedly asked to dwell on the frontier.
idiomatic: His heart was vengeance; he repeatedly asked the border.

literal: In the Shengui era he was Area Commander and Inspector of Xuzhou and Grand General of the Cavalry.
idiomatic: In Shengui he was Xuzhou commander and Grand General of Cavalry.

literal: He then raised a school east of Qing, and on the first and fifteenth of the month summoned local gentry's sons, received them with kind face, and discussed the classics with them.
idiomatic: He raised a school east of Qing and on the first and fifteenth summoned local sons to discuss the classics.

literal: Diligent in hearing cases, clerks and people loved him.
idiomatic: Diligent in judgment, clerks and people loved him.

literal: In the second year of Zhengguang he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Zhengguang year 2 he was summoned as Left Secretariat Vice Director.

literal: Skilled in clerical duty, he had a great reputation.
idiomatic: Skilled in office work, he won great fame.

literal: In the fourth year he memorialized, saying:
idiomatic: In year 4 he memorialized:

literal: I reflect that the names civil and martial stand at the utmost of men;
idiomatic: I reflect that civil and martial names stand at men's utmost;

literal: the title of virtue and conduct is the foremost of life.
idiomatic: virtue and conduct are life's foremost titles.

literal: The beauty of loyalty and integrity is the praise of standing at court;
idiomatic: Loyalty and integrity are praise at court;

literal: the name of benevolence and righteousness is the beginning of comporting oneself.
idiomatic: benevolence and righteousness begin personal conduct.

literal: Unless one's office is among the nine ministers and one's charge is the four mountains, with appointment saying "you shall harmonize" and yielding called "we go," how can one bear the great name and fulfill this fine repute?
idiomatic: Unless one holds the nine ministries or the four mountains' charge—with "you shall harmonize" in appointment and "we go" in yielding—how bear the great name and fulfill fine repute?

literal: From recent times, office knows no high or low, man knows no noble or base—all adorn words with borrowed talk and use it to praise and lift one another.
idiomatic: Lately, high or low, noble or base—all polish borrowed phrases to praise each other.

literal: Those who ask cannot measure how much; those who give cannot verify right and wrong; thus cap and shoe are traded, name and reality both lost.
idiomatic: Givers cannot verify truth; caps and shoes trade places; name and fact both fail.

literal: Calling it examination of merit, the affair is like indiscriminate promotion—confused and boundless, how can it be told!
idiomatic: Merit review becomes indiscriminate promotion—endless confusion, beyond telling!

literal: Again, officials in the capital accumulate ten years of examinations.
idiomatic: Again, capital officials pile ten years of reviews.

literal: Among them, some have had masters they served shift three or four times;
idiomatic: Some have served masters who shifted three or four times;
